rationale.C: Tier C faces a high-severity breach risk due to firmware-induced reboots on 30% of nodes, with an estimated 0.15% monthly availability loss over six weeks and a confirmed SLA breach in the trailing data (99.44%). The platform policy flags utilization at 43% and headroom at 36.4%, both below thresholds; no capacity trigger yet. Spend for firmware fix is scheduled Q4, with effect starting in Week 1 of Q4 due to a four-week lead time. If unaddressed, Tier C will breach SLA by month 2 of the next quarter and face sustained degradation.
rationale.A: Tier A shows a clear trend of declining availability (99.97 → 99.95 → 99.91) and is projected to fall below 99.90% in the next quarter's first month under current trajectory (-0.06%/month). With 9% QoQ traffic growth, utilization will rise from 71% to 84% by Month 3 (calculated as 71 + 9*3 = 98%, but actual utilization is 71% at start; extrapolated with 9% growth: 71 * (1.09)^3 ≈ 85%). At 85% utilization, Tier A will hit the 75% capacity trigger in Month 4. Headroom remains at 12.4%, but sustained throughput is near design limit. Spend for node refresh is scheduled Q4 with effect starting in Week 6 of Q4 (10-week lead time). Without action, Tier A will breach SLA and exceed utilization guardrail by Month 4.
rationale.B: Tier B has no current breach or capacity trigger; utilization at 58% remains below 75%, headroom at 48.2% is sufficient. The only risk is a planned firmware rollout next quarter costing 0.02% monthly availability, which will reduce overall platform availability by 0.06% over the quarter. No immediate capacity or SLA risk; investment priority lower due to stable metrics and low exposure.
